newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebel leader wants talks on power handover.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebel leader wants talks on power handover.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Wednesday gave ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko just over two weeks to agree to negotiations on handover of power or face a major rebel offensive.

Kabila, speaking to Reuters at an opulent lakeside residence formerly occupied by Mobutu, also accused France and Belgium of recruiting and funding some 300 foreign mercenaries to back the ragged government army.
Kabila is the head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), a coalition of rebel groups ranged against Mobutu.
"Mobutu has until February 21 to come to the table and talk on relinquishing power, otherwise he will face a major offensive to remove him," said Kabila, surrounded by gun-toting bodyguards.
He added: "Unless Mobutu can come to the table and agree to relinquish power, I will have him removed by military force. The only option left for Mobutu is to negotiate a handover."

In nearly four months of fighting, Kabila's forces have taken a swath of eastern Zaire stretching more than 1,000 km (600 miles) almost from the Zambian border in the south up towards Sudan and Uganda in the north.

The confident rebel leader, buoyed by recent battlefield victories, said that in the south his forces had advanced to within 40 km (25 miles) of the town of Moba, which is on the road to Lubumbashi, capital of the mineral-rich Shaba province. Moba and Lubumbashi are about 500 km (300 miles) apart.

Kabila said other frontline units were within 19 km (11 miles) of Lubutu and were besieging the town, main base for Rwanda's 40,000-strong ousted Hutu army. Capture of Lubutu would bring Kabila's forces within short range of Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city and base for foreign mercenaries.

"We are 40 km outside Moba and other units are surrounding the town. But this must not be considered as a major advance. We are only dealing with threats from Zaire's useless army," Mobutu's veteran foe said.
Kabila said his forces had also captured the northeastern towns of Mambasa and Watsa. Until five days ago Watsa was a strong base for the mercenaries brought in to help reverse rebel gains.
He said rebels had cut off government troops at the eastern town of Shabunda, where aid workers say an estimated 35,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees have very little food left.
"We are putting pressure on Mobutu and his useless army. We have not met much resistance because Mobutu's army does not have generals, they are traders," Kabila said.
He accused France and Belgium of recruiting the mercenaries and paying for them. Kabila said seven mercenaries had already been killed in battles with his troops.

"France and Belgium are recruiting and paying for the mercenaries. But be assured they will be defeated because the population is on my side," Kabila added. France and Belgium deny they are the paymasters for Mobutu's hired guns.
Kabila poured scorn on reports that Zaire was preparing to receive troops from allies Togo, Chad and Morocco, saying "they will all be killed here, they will be defeated."
He denied Zairean accusations that Rwanda and Uganda were backing him, saying his war was a people's campaign against a longtime dictatorship.
"People are tired of Mobutu's slavery system. They are tired of being abused by a corrupt and unworthy political system. They are now joining us in their hundreds of thousands," he said.
